accepted.s: The two-step devaluation of the Indian rupee during the 1991 crisis was carried out on:
accepted.x: The rupee was devalued in two steps on 1 July and 3 July 1991. The devaluation was nearly 20 percent and was intended, among other things, to make exports cheaper and address the balance of payments problem.
accepted.tq: Use the precise dates and distinguish the crisis-response measure from later reforms.
accepted.sec: Crisis-response measures - taken and not taken

accepted.s: The principal immediate purpose of the 1991 rupee devaluation was to:
o: Increase the price of Indian exports in foreign markets
Make Indian exports cheaper and help correct the balance of payments
Finance the fiscal deficit through currency expansion
accepted.x: Devaluation makes domestic goods relatively cheaper for foreign buyers and was undertaken to help address the balance of payments crisis.
accepted.tq: Apply the economic effect of devaluation rather than recall only its date.
accepted.sec: Crisis-response measures - taken and not taken

accepted.s: During the 1991 balance of payments crisis, approximately how much gold was pledged by India to obtain external support?
accepted.x: India airlifted and pledged approximately 67 tonnes of gold. The gold was sent to the Bank of England and UBS; the Bank of Japan is also mentioned in connection with the transaction.
accepted.tq: Test the crisis figure through closely spaced numerical options.
accepted.sec: Crisis-response measures - taken and not taken

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence concerning exchange-rate and account convertibility reforms?
o: Capital account convertibility was achieved in 1991, followed by current account convertibility in 1993.
Current account convertibility preceded devaluation in 1990.
The exchange rate became market-determined in 1993, while current account convertibility came in 1994; full capital account convertibility was not undertaken.
Both current and capital account convertibility were introduced in 1991.
accepted.x: The exchange rate became market-determined in 1993 and current account convertibility came later, in 1994. Full capital account convertibility was not undertaken.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely related exchange-rate, current-account and capital-account measures.
accepted.sec: Crisis-response measures - taken and not taken

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a component of India's 1991 crisis-response package?
accepted.x: Demonetisation was not part of the 1991 crisis-response package. India's demonetisation measures referred to here were undertaken in 1978 and 2016.
accepted.tq: Identify the measure belonging to a different policy episode.
accepted.sec: Crisis-response measures - taken and not taken

accepted.s: The Finance Minister associated with the initiation of the 1991 economic reforms was:
accepted.x: Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister during the initiation of the 1991 reforms. The period is often described as the Manmohan-Rao era.
accepted.tq: Use the office-holder and distinguish him from reform committee chairpersons.
accepted.sec: Reform architects - PM, FM, labels, committees

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: P.V. Narasimha Rao — architect of liberalisation; Dr. Manmohan Singh — Prime Minister in June 1991
P.V. Narasimha Rao — father of Indian economic reforms; Dr. Manmohan Singh — architect or pioneer of liberalisation
P.V. Narasimha Rao — Chairman of the Malhotra Committee; Dr. Manmohan Singh — Chairman of the MRTP Commission
P.V. Narasimha Rao — Finance Minister in 1991; Dr. Manmohan Singh — Chairman of the Raja Chelliah Committee
accepted.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao is widely called the father of Indian economic reforms, while Dr. Manmohan Singh is regarded as the architect or pioneer of liberalisation.
accepted.tq: Check the person-title association before accepting the complete pair.
accepted.sec: Reform architects - PM, FM, labels, committees

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
a. Narasimham Committee
b. Raja Chelliah Committee
c. Rangarajan Committee
 d. Malhotra Committee
List-II (Area)
i. Insurance reform
ii. Tax reform
iii. Financial-sector reform
iv. PSU disinvestment
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The Narasimham Committee dealt with financial-sector reform; the Raja Chelliah Committee with tax reform; the Rangarajan Committee with PSU disinvestment; and the Malhotra Committee with insurance reform.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive committee-area pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: Reform architects - PM, FM, labels, committees

accepted.s: The Narasimham Committee of 1991 was primarily concerned with:
o: Industrial licensing and foreign trade quotas
Financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and private banks
accepted.x: The Narasimham Committee focused on financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and the development of private banks such as HDFC and ICICI.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the committee's sector from neighbouring reform committees.
accepted.sec: Reform architects - PM, FM, labels, committees

accepted.s: The Raja Chelliah Committee is associated with recommendations for:
o: Lower peak tax rates and a wider tax base
accepted.x: The Raja Chelliah Committee dealt with tax reform and recommended lower peak rates along with a wider tax base.
accepted.tq: Link the committee to its precise reform objective.
accepted.sec: Reform architects - PM, FM, labels, committees

accepted.s: Which of the following was an immediate trigger of India's 1991 economic crisis?
o: The widening of the world export share of India
The long-term operation of the MRTP Act of 1970
The gradual expansion of public investment returns
The Gulf War, which doubled oil prices and dried up Gulf remittances
accepted.x: The Gulf War in August 1990 doubled oil prices and reduced Gulf remittances, creating an immediate external pressure on India.
accepted.tq: Separate an immediate external shock from structural domestic causes.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s: Political instability contributed to the 1991 crisis because:
o: India changed governments twice between December 1989 and June 1991, followed by the fall of the Chandra Shekhar government
The Union government abolished all state governments during the period
The political crisis began only after the reforms were completed
A single government remained in office without interruption from 1989 to 1991
accepted.x: Two changes of government occurred between December 1989 and June 1991, and the Chandra Shekhar government subsequently fell, adding to uncertainty and instability.
accepted.tq: Use the chronology and duration to identify the correct political trigger.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations contains only immediate triggers of the 1991 crisis?
1. Gulf War and rise in oil prices
2. NRI deposit flight
3. Collapse of the Soviet Union
4. Fiscal profligacy from the Sixth to the Seventh Plan
accepted.x: The Gulf War, NRI deposit flight and the collapse of the Soviet Union were immediate external or political-economic triggers. Fiscal profligacy was a long-term structural cause.
accepted.tq: Classify each item by time horizon instead of merely recognising its association with the crisis.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s: The collapse of the Soviet Union in December 1991 affected India primarily by:
o: Providing a new source of concessional oil imports
Increasing India's share in world exports
Ending the need for foreign exchange reserves
accepted.x: The Soviet Union had been an important trading partner of India; its collapse weakened that trading relationship during the crisis period.
accepted.tq: Identify the direct external-trade consequence of a geopolitical event.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents a long-term cause rather than an immediate trigger of the 1991 crisis?
o: Persistent fiscal profligacy and rising fiscal deficit
accepted.x: Persistent fiscal profligacy was a long-term domestic structural cause. The other three were immediate external-financing or geopolitical pressures.
accepted.tq: Find the structural domestic factor among short-term external shocks.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s: India's gross fiscal deficit increased from 5.4 percent of GDP in 1981-82 to approximately what level in 1989-90?
accepted.x: The gross fiscal deficit rose from 5.4 percent in 1981-82 to 8.0 percent in 1989-90. The average also increased from 6.3 percent during the Sixth Plan to 8.2 percent during the Seventh Plan.
accepted.tq: Distinguish endpoint values from plan-period averages.
accepted.sec: Causes of the crisis - immediate vs long-term

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of the economic groundwork laid during the 1980s?
o: Complete abolition of all industrial licensing
Broad-banding of licences and easier imports of capital goods
accepted.x: The 1980s saw broad-banding of licences, easier capital-goods imports, a higher MRTP limit and relaxation of FERA. Complete delicensing and FEMA came later.
accepted.tq: Distinguish preparatory 1980s measures from post-1991 reforms.
accepted.sec: Starting point of liberalisation - 1980s groundwork, what came first

accepted.s: During the 1980s groundwork for liberalisation, the MRTP asset limit was raised to:
accepted.x: The MRTP asset limit was raised to ₹100 crore during the 1980s reform groundwork.
accepted.tq: Test the exact threshold through adjacent monetary values.
accepted.sec: Starting point of liberalisation - 1980s groundwork, what came first

accepted.s: The growth rate during the 1980s was described as debt-fuelled because growth:
o: Resulted from the abolition of all public-sector enterprises
Broke the Hindu rate and reached about 5.5 percent while relying on increased borrowing
Was generated entirely by agricultural exports
Remained below the earlier Hindu rate throughout the decade
accepted.x: Growth broke the earlier Hindu rate and touched about 5.5 percent, but the expansion was debt-fuelled rather than based entirely on sustainable internal resources.
accepted.tq: Combine the growth figure with the qualification attached to it.
accepted.sec: Starting point of liberalisation - 1980s groundwork, what came first

accepted.s:
Arrange the following measures in the order in which they occurred during the initial 1991 reform sequence:
A. Industrial delicensing
B. Devaluation of the rupee
C. Removal of import quotas and EXIM scrips
D. Market-determined exchange rate
accepted.x: Devaluation came first in July 1991, followed by industrial delicensing, removal of EXIM scrips and import quotas, and the market-determined exchange rate in 1993.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the intervening reform measures.
accepted.sec: Starting point of liberalisation - 1980s groundwork, what came first

accepted.s: After the 1991 reforms, industrial licensing was abolished for all but approximately:
accepted.x: Industrial licensing was abolished for all but five or six industries. This formed a central part of industrial delicensing.
accepted.tq: Test the narrow exception to a broad reform statement.
accepted.sec: Starting point of liberalisation - 1980s groundwork, what came first

accepted.s:
Which of the following was included in the fiscal policy measures of 1991?
1. Control of public expenditure
2. Curtailment of grants and subsidies
3. Better tax collection
4. Contraction of the tax net
accepted.x: The fiscal package included expenditure control, reduction of grants and subsidies and improved tax collection. The tax net was widened rather than contracted.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed tax-net statement while retaining the other fiscal measures.
accepted.sec: 1991 fiscal policy measures - included and excluded

accepted.s: The tax reform approach associated with the 1991 fiscal measures emphasised:
o: Lower peak income-tax and corporate-tax rates
Higher peak income-tax and corporate-tax rates
A narrow tax base with fewer taxpayers
accepted.x: The reform approach associated with the Chelliah Committee favoured lower peak income-tax and corporate-tax rates along with a wider tax base.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of tax-rate reform and distinguish it from tax-base expansion.
accepted.sec: 1991 fiscal policy measures - included and excluded

accepted.s: The post-1991 trade orientation represented a shift from:
o: Foreign investment to complete capital controls
accepted.x: Economic policy shifted from import substitution towards export promotion, supported by lower tariffs and greater openness to foreign investment.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed policy-direction pair directly.
accepted.sec: Post-reform direction - global integration, private sector

accepted.s: Which of the following developments correctly reflects the post-1991 reform direction?
o: FDI and FPI were invited, while IT and services exports provided an important cushion
FDI was prohibited and services exports were discouraged
Tariffs were raised uniformly to protect all domestic producers
Export promotion was replaced by a complete ban on imports
accepted.x: The post-reform approach lowered tariffs, invited foreign direct and portfolio investment, and benefited from IT and services exports as a cushion.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the complementary openness measures without an absolute claim.
accepted.sec: Post-reform direction - global integration, private sector

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the institutional changes after the 1991 reforms?
o: SEBI became statutory in 1992 and FERA was replaced by FEMA in 1999
SEBI became statutory in 1999 and FEMA replaced FERA in 1992
SEBI was abolished in 1992 and FERA was strengthened in 1999
SEBI became statutory in 1991 and FEMA replaced FERA in 1994
accepted.x: SEBI received statutory status in 1992, while FEMA replaced FERA in 1999.
accepted.tq: Pair each institution with its correct year and avoid swapping the two dates.
accepted.sec: Post-reform direction - global integration, private sector

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the National Renewal Fund was to:
o: Finance voluntary retirement, retraining and redeployment of displaced workers
Provide foreign exchange to importing firms
accepted.x: The Fund financed voluntary retirement schemes, retraining and redeployment for workers displaced by restructuring or closure of industrial units.
accepted.tq: Recognise the social-safety-net function from the worker-displacement scenario.
accepted.sec: National Renewal Fund - objectives, workers covered

accepted.s: Which workers were primarily covered by the National Renewal Fund?
o: Organised-sector workers, mainly in public-sector undertakings
Only foreign employees of multinational companies
All informal workers irrespective of industrial restructuring
accepted.x: The Fund covered organised-sector workers, particularly those employed in public-sector undertakings affected by restructuring or closure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the organised-sector target group from an excessively broad coverage claim.
accepted.sec: National Renewal Fund - objectives, workers covered

accepted.s: The National Renewal Fund was wound up in:
accepted.x: The National Renewal Fund, established in February 1992, was wound up in 2000.
accepted.tq: Use the lifecycle sequence of a scheme to identify its closing year.
accepted.sec: National Renewal Fund - objectives, workers covered

accepted.s: Which sector was significantly reshaped by post-1991 reforms through private and foreign entry and falling prices?
accepted.x: Telecommunications was substantially reshaped by private and foreign entry, which contributed to falling prices.
accepted.tq: Match the reform effect with the sector that experienced direct competition.
accepted.sec: Sectors reshaped by reforms vs largely untouched

accepted.s: Which one of the following sectors remained largely a state monopoly after the reforms?
accepted.x: Railways remained a state monopoly, although modernisation continued to be pursued. The other sectors experienced greater private-sector participation or competition.
accepted.tq: Find the sector that was comparatively untouched among reform-exposed industries.
accepted.sec: Sectors reshaped by reforms vs largely untouched

accepted.s: Which pair correctly represents a sector reshaped by reforms and a sector where reform remained slow, respectively?
accepted.x: Banking was reshaped through private banks and interest deregulation, whereas agriculture experienced little direct reform.
accepted.tq: Compare one transformed sector with one sector largely outside the direct reform process.
accepted.sec: Sectors reshaped by reforms vs largely untouched

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding sectors affected by post-1991 reforms?
1. Civil aviation saw the entry of private airlines.
2. Automobiles and consumer electronics were reshaped by reforms.
3. Power distribution underwent complete and uncontested privatisation.
4. Major ports were only recently undergoing corporatisation.
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: Private airlines entered civil aviation, and automobiles and consumer electronics were reshaped by reforms. Power-distribution privatisation remained debated, while corporatisation of major ports was only recently progressing.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim of complete privatisation while retaining the sectoral comparisons.
accepted.sec: Sectors reshaped by reforms vs largely untouched

accepted.s: Abolition of industrial licensing and granting firms greater freedom in determining prices are measures that primarily promote:
accepted.x: Liberalisation means reducing state control over economic activity. Abolition of licensing and price freedom are typical liberalisation measures.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy label from the nature of the state-control reduction.
accepted.sec: Meaning of L, P and G - which policy each action promotes

accepted.s: Opening previously protected sectors to private firms and selling government holdings in public-sector enterprises primarily promote:
accepted.x: Privatisation involves enlarging the role of private firms, including through disinvestment and the sale of public-sector enterprises.
accepted.tq: Distinguish ownership change from general deregulation and international integration.
accepted.sec: Meaning of L, P and G - which policy each action promotes

accepted.s: Which combination most directly represents globalisation in the context of the 1991 reforms?
o: Abolition of domestic industrial licensing and price controls only
Disinvestment of public enterprises without foreign trade reform
Entry of multinational companies, reduction of import duties and freer movement of capital and technology
Expansion of state ownership and restriction of foreign technology
accepted.x: Globalisation involves integration with the world economy through multinational-company entry, lower import duties and freer flows of capital and technology.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing international-integration measures rather than domestic ownership reforms.
accepted.sec: Meaning of L, P and G - which policy each action promotes

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the relationship among liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
o: Privatisation is the outcome of globalisation, while liberalisation means only export promotion.
Liberalisation and privatisation prohibit the international flow of technology.
Globalisation is an outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, with outsourcing as a major feature.
Globalisation is independent of both liberalisation and privatisation, and outsourcing is unrelated to it.
accepted.x: Globalisation is described as an outcome of liberalisation and privatisation. Outsourcing is a major feature associated with globalisation.
accepted.tq: Test the relationship among the three policy terms and the associated feature of outsourcing.
accepted.sec: Meaning of L, P and G - which policy each action promotes
